title: U.S. House · California's 26th District
area: Most of Ventura County and a small portion of Los Angeles County, including Thousand Oaks, Oxnard, Camarillo, Santa Paula, Moorpark, Westlake Village, and part of Simi Valley. District lines were redrawn for the 2026 election under California Proposition 50.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 election cycle after voters approved Proposition 50 on November 4, 2025, a mid-decade redistricting measure.

This is an open seat: incumbent Democrat Julia Brownley did not seek re-election to this district in 2026. Democrat Jacqui Irwin, currently a member of the California State Assembly, won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 41.3% of the vote; Republican Samuel Gallucci advanced with 20.9%.

candidates.name: Jacqui Irwin
candidates.currentRole: Member, California State Assembly, District 42 (since 2022; term ends December 2026)
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 primary with 41.3% of the vote

summary.text: Jacqui Irwin is the Democratic nominee for California's 26th Congressional District, an open seat. She is a systems engineer and currently represents California's 42nd Assembly District; she previously served on the Thousand Oaks City Council, including two terms as mayor.

background.text: Born in Woodland Hills, California; graduated from Taft High School and earned a bachelor of science in systems engineering from UC San Diego in 1985.
Worked as an engineer at Teledyne Systems and at Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Lab.
Elected to the Thousand Oaks City Council in 2004 and served two terms as mayor of Thousand Oaks before her election to the State Assembly.

positions.summary: At a Sept. 25 League of Women Voters debate, said she would pursue stronger red-flag laws and expanded background checks.
At the Sept. 25 debate, said Congress should have a greater role in decisions to enter war and criticized the Iran military campaign.
At the Sept. 25 debate, called ICE a lawless agency and criticized its enforcement practices, and supported a pathway to citizenship for longtime farmworkers.
positions.quote: I think ICE is a lawless agency

record.text: In the 2025-2026 California State Assembly session, serves as chair of the Climate Change Policies Committee and as a member of the Agriculture, Business and Professions, Privacy and Consumer Protection, Rules, Utilities and Energy, and Fairs, Allocation, and Classification committees.

candidates.name: Samuel Gallucci
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary with 20.9% of the vote

summary.text: Samuel Gallucci is the Republican nominee for California's 26th Congressional District. He previously ran for governor of California in the 2021 recall election.

background.text: Ran as a candidate in the 2021 California gubernatorial recall election.

positions.summary: At the Sept. 25 debate, said California already has strict gun laws and gun restrictions are not a high priority for people he hears from, while saying background checks and keeping guns from criminals are important.
positions.quote: some of the tightest gun laws in the country

positions.summary: At the Sept. 25 debate, said agricultural workers who have been in the country for decades should be allowed to remain and that people who are criminals should be removed.
positions.quote: All the workers need to stay. All the criminals need to go

researchNotes: Neither Jacqui Irwin nor Samuel Gallucci has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Re-checked https://ballotpedia.org/Samuel_Gallucci (September 2026): no biography section and no Candidate Connection survey for 2026 or his 2021 recall run; his campaign website (https://samgallucci.com/) again loaded with no usable text content (JavaScript-rendered). His entry stays minimal; no other public statements of his positions were found.
